```{r load}
# data from data-raw/chinook_sites_data.R and data-raw/chinook_sites_map.R
library(wet)
library(ggplot2)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)

vd <- function(f) system.file("vignette-data", f, package = "wet")
v <- readRDS(vd("chinook_sites_values.rds"))
map <- readRDS(vd("chinook_sites_map.rds"))
prov <- v$provenance
sites <- v$sites
ids <- c("maxan", "swift", "naver", "gosnell")
stopifnot(identical(sites$site_id, ids))
name_of <- stats::setNames(sites$name, sites$site_id)

# colours come from the gq registries, so no hex literal appears in this article;
# assert each class set, because a malformed CSV row adds a layer silently
reg <- gq::gq_reg_custom(system.file("cartography", "wet_station.csv", package = "wet"))
reg_main <- gq::gq_reg_main()
classes <- function(layer, expect) {
  x <- gq::gq_tmap_classes(reg$layers[[layer]])
  stopifnot(identical(names(x$values), expect))
  list(values = x$values, labels = stats::setNames(x$labels, names(x$values)))
}
pal_map <- classes("chinook_sites_map", c("box", "target_gauged", "target_ungauged", "donor"))
pal_change <- classes("chinook_sites_change", c("extended", "carried"))
pal_window <- classes("chinook_sites_window", c("migration", "spawning", "flow"))
pal_series <- classes("chinook_sites_series", c("band", "measured", "filled", "borrowed", "period_mean"))
stream_sty <- reg_main$layers$streams_all$classification$classes$WA24111110
lake_sty <- reg_main$layers$lake
town_sty <- reg_main$layers$town

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
            theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
pct <- function(x) paste0(round(abs(x)), "%")
pct_of <- function(z) 100 * (exp(z) - 1)
and_text <- function(x) sub(", ([^,]*)$", " and \\1", paste(x, collapse = ", "))
md_text <- function(md) {
  d <- as.Date(paste0("2001-", md))
  sprintf("%s %d", format(d, "%B"), as.integer(format(d, "%d")))
}
# the windows every site ran under (the Bulkley's), from the bundle
wb <- unique(v$windows[v$windows$group == "BULK", c("window", "start", "end")])
stopifnot(identical(wb$window, c("migration", "spawning")))
wlab <- stats::setNames(sprintf("%s (%s – %s)", c("Migration", "Spawning"), md_text(wb$start), md_text(wb$end)),
                        wb$window)
```

```{r numbers}
ch <- v$change
ch$pct <- pct_of(ch$change)
ch$pct_lo <- pct_of(ch$lo)
ch$pct_hi <- pct_of(ch$hi)
row_of <- function(id, w, route, s = "mean", group = "BULK") {
  r <- ch[ch$site_id == id & ch$group == group & ch$statistic == s & ch$window == w & ch$route == route, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  r
}
spw <- do.call(rbind, lapply(ids, row_of, w = "spawning", route = "carried"))
stopifnot(all(spw$pct < 0))
low_spw <- spw[spw$pct_hi < 0, ]
# the opening: Maxan measured for five summers; Gosnell never gauged; Swift and Naver under twenty
stopifnot(sites$obs_n[sites$site_id == "maxan"] == 5, identical(sites$kind, c("extend", "extend", "extend", "ungauged")),
          all(sites$obs_n[sites$site_id %in% c("swift", "naver")] < 20))
# "no stream's mean flow shows a clear change by either route" in the migration window, both window sets
mig_all <- ch[ch$statistic == "mean" & ch$window == "migration", ]
stopifnot(all(mig_all$pct_lo < 0), all(mig_all$pct_hi > 0))
# "since 2011": every route's years since 2011 run to 2024 or 2025
stopifnot(all(ch$n_post %in% 14:15))
# held-out scores by window, from the reports' tables, under the Bulkley windows
ssc <- v$score_settings[v$score_settings$group == "BULK", ]
ss_mig <- ssc[ssc$setting == "migration mean, k = 5", ]
ss_spw <- ssc[ssc$setting == "spawning mean", ]
stopifnot(setequal(ss_mig$site_id, ids), setequal(ss_spw$site_id, ids))
# "below the bar ... at all four" under the Bulkley windows; the migration window at or over it in both sets
# "scores worse in the spawning window than in the migration window at all four" (the Bulkley windows)
stopifnot(all(ss_spw$carried[match(ids, ss_spw$site_id)] < ss_mig$carried[match(ids, ss_mig$site_id)]))
stopifnot(all(ss_spw$carried < 0.5), all(ss_mig$carried >= 0.5),
          all(v$score_settings$carried[v$score_settings$setting == "migration mean, k = 5"] >= 0.5))
sc <- v$scores[v$scores$group == "BULK", ]
stopifnot(identical(sc$site_id, ids))
# "about as well across the Cottonwood, Morice and Bulkley boxes, and worse in the upper Fraser":
# Naver and Gosnell within 0.15 of Maxan on both routes in both windows; Swift's filled-in record 0.2 or more below
ss_of <- function(id, setting, col) ssc[[col]][ssc$site_id == id & ssc$setting == setting]
for (st in c("migration mean, k = 5", "spawning mean")) {
  for (id in c("naver", "gosnell")) {
    stopifnot(abs(ss_of(id, st, "ols") - ss_of("maxan", st, "ols")) <= 0.15,
              abs(ss_of(id, st, "carried") - ss_of("maxan", st, "carried")) <= 0.15)
  }
  stopifnot(ss_of("swift", st, "ols") <= ss_of("maxan", st, "ols") - 0.2)
}
# "the windows are the Bulkley's at all four; only the Morice has its own"
stopifnot(all(grepl("^BULK", sites$windows)), identical(sites$windows != "BULK", sites$site_id == "gosnell"))
```

Many streams that matter to salmon were gauged for only a few summers, or never. This
article uses the R package [`wet`](https://newgraphenvironment.github.io/wet/) to ask how
their summer flow has changed since before 1981, at four streams in northern British
Columbia that Chinook salmon use: Maxan Creek, with five full summers on record; Swift
Creek and Naver Creek, with `r sites$obs_n[sites$site_id == "swift"]` and
`r sites$obs_n[sites$site_id == "naver"]`; and Gosnell Creek, never gauged. Each is run the
same way, with the method fixed before any result, and each is scored on how well the
method predicts gauges it was not given.

**The answer.** In the salmon spawning window, a stream's mean flow in a typical year since
2011 was lower than before 1981 at all four streams, by `r pct(min(abs(spw$pct)))` to
`r pct(max(abs(spw$pct)))` from nearby gauges' departures; at
`r and_text(sub(" Creek$", "", name_of[low_spw$site_id]))` creeks that route's 90% range
stays below no change. In the migration window no stream's mean flow shows a clear change.
Borrowing departures, the one route every stream has, scores worse in the spawning window
than in the migration window at all four under these windows.

## Where are the four streams?

```{r where}
tg <- map$targets
stopifnot(setequal(tg$site_id, ids))
t_of <- function(id) tg[tg$site_id == id, ]
pl_of <- function(name) {
  p <- map$places[map$places$name == name, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(p) >= 1)
  p[1, ]
}
# the compass point and distance from a place to a stream, as the orientation states them
compass <- function(name, id) {
  a <- sf::st_coordinates(pl_of(name))
  b <- c(t_of(id)$mouth_x, t_of(id)$mouth_y)   # where the stream joins its river, as the sentence says
  deg <- (atan2(b[1] - a[1], b[2] - a[2]) * 180 / pi) %% 360
  c("north", "north-east", "east", "south-east", "south", "south-west", "west", "north-west")[(round(deg / 45) %% 8) + 1]
}
km <- function(name, id) {
  a <- sf::st_coordinates(pl_of(name))
  sqrt((a[1] - t_of(id)$mouth_x)^2 + (a[2] - t_of(id)$mouth_y)^2) / 1000
}
# the rivers each stream flows into, from the Freshwater Atlas
stopifnot(t_of("maxan")$into1 == "Bulkley River", t_of("maxan")$into2 == "Skeena River",
          t_of("gosnell")$into1 == "Thautil River", t_of("gosnell")$into2 == "Morice River",
          t_of("naver")$into1 == "Fraser River", t_of("swift")$into1 == "McLennan River",
          t_of("swift")$into2 == "Fraser River")
# "two in the Skeena system and two in the Fraser", from the top of each stream's watershed code; one map for each
stopifnot(identical(sort(tg$site_id[tg$system == "Skeena River"]), c("gosnell", "maxan")),
          identical(sort(tg$site_id[tg$system == "Fraser River"]), c("naver", "swift")),
          identical(sort(tg$site_id[tg$map == "skeena"]), c("gosnell", "maxan")),
          identical(sort(tg$site_id[tg$map == "fraser"]), c("naver", "swift")))
# measured from each mouth: "near Topley, south-east of Smithers"; "south-west of Houston";
# "near Hixon, south of Prince George"; "at Valemount"
stopifnot(km("Topley", "maxan") < 25, compass("Smithers", "maxan") == "south-east",
          compass("Houston", "gosnell") == "south-west",
          km("Hixon", "naver") < 10, compass("Prince George", "naver") == "south", km("Valemount", "swift") < 5)
# every box the same size
stopifnot(all(abs(sites$lon_span - sites$lon_span[1]) < 1e-9), all(abs(sites$lat_span - sites$lat_span[1]) < 1e-9))
```

The four streams are in northern British Columbia, two in the Skeena system and two in
the Fraser. Maxan Creek flows into the upper Bulkley River near Topley, south-east of
Smithers, and Gosnell Creek into the Thautil River just above the Morice River,
south-west of Houston. Naver Creek flows into the Fraser River near Hixon, south of Prince
George, and Swift Creek into the McLennan River, a Fraser tributary, at Valemount. Each
borrows its numbers from gauges inside a box of the same size around it.

```{r region-data}
map_w <- 7
map_h <- 6.1   # a map area of attr(map, "map_asp") above a legend of about 0.7 in
stopifnot(abs(map_w / (map_h - 0.7) - attr(map, "map_asp")) < 0.01)
region <- function(m) {
  ext <- sf::st_bbox(map$extents[map$extents$map == m, ])
  ex <- ext[["xmax"]] - ext[["xmin"]]
  ey <- ext[["ymax"]] - ext[["ymin"]]
  cx <- (ext[["xmin"]] + ext[["xmax"]]) / 2
  s <- map$streams[map$streams$map == m, ]
  g <- map$gauges[map$gauges$map == m, ]
  g <- g[!duplicated(g$station_number), ]
  g$part <- "donor"
  t <- tg[tg$map == m, ]
  t$part <- ifelse(t$kind == "extend", "target_gauged", "target_ungauged")
  txy <- sf::st_coordinates(t)
  pl <- map$places[map$places$map == m, ]
  pxy <- sf::st_coordinates(pl)
  # the rivers the orientation names, each labelled midway along its longest drawn part
  rv <- s[s$gnis_name %in% stats::na.omit(unique(c(t$into1, t$into2))) & !s$main, ]
  rv <- rv[!duplicated(rv$gnis_name), ]
  rxy <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(rv)), function(k) {
    parts <- sf::st_cast(sf::st_geometry(rv[k, ]), "LINESTRING")
    longest <- parts[which.max(as.numeric(sf::st_length(parts)))]
    sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_line_sample(longest, sample = 0.5))[1, 1:2]
  }))
  # every label in one repelling layer, so none covers another or a marker; a white halo keeps each readable
  lab <- rbind(
    data.frame(x = txy[, 1], y = txy[, 2], label = t$name, face = "bold", size = 3.5, col = "black"),
    data.frame(x = pxy[, 1], y = pxy[, 2], label = pl$name, face = "plain", size = 3.1, col = town_sty$label$color),
    if (nrow(rv)) data.frame(x = rxy[, 1], y = rxy[, 2], label = rv$gnis_name, face = "italic", size = 3,
                             col = lake_sty$stroke$color),
    # empty labels: the mouths and the gauges, which every label keeps clear of
    data.frame(x = t$mouth_x, y = t$mouth_y, label = "", face = "plain", size = 3, col = "black"),
    data.frame(x = sf::st_coordinates(g)[, 1], y = sf::st_coordinates(g)[, 2], label = "", face = "plain", size = 3,
               col = "black"))
  sb_km <- max(gq::gq_scale_breaks(ext))
  sb <- data.frame(x = ext[["xmax"]] - 0.04 * ex - sb_km * 1000, y = ext[["ymin"]] + 0.05 * ey)
  sb$xend <- sb$x + sb_km * 1000
  # the keymap: the province, and this map's frame on it
  key <- ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = map$bc, fill = "white", colour = pal_series$values[["filled"]], linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_sf(data = map$extents[map$extents$map == m, ], fill = NA, colour = pal_map$values[["target_gauged"]],
            linewidth = 0.6) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = pal_series$values[["filled"]], linewidth = 0.3))
  key_w <- 0.22 * ex
  key_h <- key_w * 1.05
  key_left <- mean(txy[, 1]) > cx   # the keymap in the corner away from the streams
  kx <- if (key_left) c(ext[["xmin"]] + 0.02 * ex, ext[["xmin"]] + 0.02 * ex + key_w) else
    c(ext[["xmax"]] - 0.02 * ex - key_w, ext[["xmax"]] - 0.02 * ex)
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = map$lakes[map$lakes$map == m, ], fill = lake_sty$fill$color, colour = lake_sty$stroke$color,
            linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_sf(data = s[!s$main, ], colour = stream_sty$color, linewidth = 0.45) +
    geom_sf(data = merge(s[s$main, ], sf::st_drop_geometry(t[c("blue_line_key", "part")])), aes(colour = part),
            linewidth = 1.1, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_sf(data = g, aes(colour = part), size = 1.5) +
    geom_sf(data = t, aes(colour = part), size = 3.2) +
    geom_point(data = data.frame(x = pxy[, 1], y = pxy[, 2]), aes(x, y), shape = 15, size = 1.3,
               colour = town_sty$label$color) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = lab, aes(x, y, label = label, fontface = face, size = I(size), colour = I(col)),
                             seed = 126, min.segment.length = Inf, box.padding = 0.35, point.padding = 0.25,
                             bg.colour = "white", bg.r = 0.12, max.overlaps = Inf, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_segment(data = sb, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y), linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_text(data = sb, aes(x = (x + xend) / 2, y = y, label = paste(sb_km, "km")), vjust = -0.7, size = 3) +
    annotation_custom(ggplotGrob(key), xmin = kx[1], xmax = kx[2], ymin = ext[["ymax"]] - 0.02 * ey - key_h,
                      ymax = ext[["ymax"]] - 0.02 * ey) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = pal_map$values, labels = pal_map$labels[c(unique(t$part), "donor")],
                        breaks = c(unique(t$part), "donor"), name = NULL) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(ext[["xmin"]], ext[["xmax"]]), ylim = c(ext[["ymin"]], ext[["ymax"]]), expand = FALSE,
             datum = NA) +
    theme_void(base_size = 10) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom", plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = pal_series$values[["band"]]),
          plot.margin = margin(4, 4, 4, 4))
}
```

```{r skeena, fig.width = map_w, fig.height = map_h, fig.cap = "Maxan and Gosnell creeks in the Skeena system, with the gauges each borrows from. The inset locates the map in British Columbia."}
region("skeena")
```

```{r fraser, fig.width = map_w, fig.height = map_h, fig.cap = "Swift and Naver creeks in the Fraser system, with the gauges each borrows from. The inset locates the map in British Columbia."}
region("fraser")

```{r use}
gauged <- sites[sites$kind == "extend" & sites$site_id != "maxan", ]
yr <- function(id, col) gauged[[col]][gauged$site_id == id]
# "inside the 1981–2010 baseline" for Swift; "before it" for Naver and Maxan
stopifnot(yr("swift", "obs_first") >= 1981, yr("swift", "obs_last") <= 2010, yr("naver", "obs_last") < 1981,
          sites$obs_last[sites$site_id == "maxan"] < 1981)
# the Chinook records, from the tracked use report
u <- v$use
use_of <- function(stream) {
  r <- u[u$stream == stream, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(r) == 1)
  r
}
sw <- use_of("Swift Creek")
nv <- use_of("Naver Creek")
gs <- use_of("Gosnell Creek")
# "in most years since 1970" and "in most years since the mid-1980s"
stopifnot(sw$nus_first == 1970, sw$nus_use_years > (sw$nus_last - sw$nus_first + 1) / 2,
          nv$nus_first %in% 1984:1986, nv$nus_use_years > (nv$nus_last - nv$nus_first + 1) / 2)
# "a major spawning site within five kilometres of its mouth"
stopifnot(any(v$use_obs$stream == "Swift Creek" & grepl("^Major spawning", v$use_obs$activity) &
                v$use_obs$measure_m < 5000))
# "one survey that found adults, in 2001, and three provincial records of fish seen"
stopifnot(gs$nus_use == 1, gs$nus_first == 2001, gs$nus_last == 2001, gs$obs == 3, gs$obs_spawning == 0)
```

Fisheries and Oceans Canada's spawner surveys find Chinook in Swift Creek in most years
since 1970, and the provincial records place a major spawning site within five kilometres
of its mouth; they find Chinook in Naver Creek in most years since the mid-1980s. Gosnell
Creek's record is thinner: one survey that found adults, in 2001, and three provincial
records of fish seen. The gauged streams' records sit in different places: Swift Creek's
`r yr("swift", "obs_n")` full summers fall between `r yr("swift", "obs_first")` and
`r yr("swift", "obs_last")`, inside the 1981–2010 baseline, while Naver Creek's
`r yr("naver", "obs_n")` fall between `r yr("naver", "obs_first")` and
`r yr("naver", "obs_last")`, before it, as do Maxan Creek's five.

## What is a window?

```{r windows-data}
d <- v$daily[v$daily$pick, ]
d$site <- factor(name_of[d$site_id], levels = name_of[ids])
day_of <- function(md) as.integer(format(as.Date(paste0("2001-", md)), "%j"))
shade <- data.frame(window = wb$window, xmin = day_of(wb$start), xmax = day_of(wb$end))
# the hydrographs show each stream's flow peaking inside the migration window and falling through spawning
peak <- vapply(ids, function(id) d$doy[d$site_id == id][which.max(d$q_m3s[d$site_id == id])], 0L)
stopifnot(all(peak >= shade$xmin[1] & peak <= shade$xmax[1]))
# "under a third of its peak": the spawning window's mean against the year's peak
low <- vapply(ids, function(id) {
  x <- d[d$site_id == id, ]
  mean(x$q_m3s[x$doy >= shade$xmin[2] & x$doy <= shade$xmax[2]]) < max(x$q_m3s) / 3
}, TRUE)
stopifnot(all(low))
month_breaks <- day_of(sprintf("%02d-01", 1:12))
```

A window is a stretch of the year when salmon use a stream for one thing. In the upper
Bulkley River, the early run of Chinook passes Moricetown Canyon before about July 30, and
Chinook spawn in August and September
([Gottesfeld and Rabnett 2007](#ref-gottesfeld2007), p. 355). This article uses the windows
New Graph's species-timing table sets for the Bulkley from that report, at all four
streams: adult migration from `r md_text(wb$start[1])` to `r md_text(wb$end[1])`, and
spawning from `r md_text(wb$start[2])` to `r md_text(wb$end[2])`. A stream's flow in a
window is its mean over those days. At every stream, flow peaks inside the migration window, as snow
melts, and is low in the spawning window, under a third of its peak.

```{r windows, fig.height = 5, fig.cap = "Each stream's typical year (1981–2010), with the two windows shaded: wet's published daily flow at the gauge, or at Gosnell Creek's mouth."}
ggplot(d) +
  geom_rect(data = shade, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = window), alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(doy, q_m3s, colour = "flow"), linewidth = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~site, scales = "free_y") +
  expand_limits(y = 0) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_window$values[c("migration", "spawning")],
                    labels = pal_window$labels[c("migration", "spawning")], name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_window$values["flow"], labels = pal_window$labels["flow"], name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = month_breaks[c(1, 4, 7, 10)], labels = month.abb[c(1, 4, 7, 10)]) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Flow (m³/s)")
```

## How has flow changed?

Two routes fill in the years a stream was not measured. Where a stream has a record,
each missing year comes from one nearby gauge, through a fit between the two streams'
flows over the years both were measured. Every stream, gauged or not, can also borrow
nearby gauges' departures from their own typical flow, year by year.

```{r years-data}
yy <- v$years[v$years$group == "BULK", ]
yy$site <- factor(name_of[yy$site_id], levels = name_of[ids])
yy$wlab <- factor(wlab[yy$window], levels = wlab)
yy$pct <- pct_of(yy$dep)
# a missing year breaks a line rather than joining across it: every series on every year of its span
yl <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(yy, list(yy$site_id, yy$window, yy$route == "borrowed"), drop = TRUE), function(x) {
  full <- data.frame(year = seq(min(x$year), max(x$year)))
  m <- merge(full, x, by = "year", all.x = TRUE)
  m$site <- x$site[1]
  m$wlab <- x$wlab[1]
  m$line <- if (x$route[1] == "borrowed") "borrowed" else "filled"
  # a year with no neighbouring year draws no line, so it gets a point
  have <- !is.na(m$dep)
  m$alone <- have & !c(FALSE, have[-length(have)]) & !c(have[-1], FALSE)
  m
}))
# 7. the change caption's "to 2024, or 2025 where recorded"
last <- tapply(yy$year, list(yy$site_id, yy$window, yy$route == "borrowed"), max)
stopifnot(all(last[!is.na(last)] %in% 2024:2025))
# the period lines: each route's mean departure before 1981 and since 2011; their difference is the change
per <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(yy, list(yy$site_id, yy$window), drop = TRUE), function(x) {
  b <- x[x$route == "borrowed", ]
  data.frame(site = x$site[1], wlab = x$wlab[1], x = c(min(b$year), 2011) - 0.5,
             xend = c(1980, max(b$year)) + 0.5,
             y = pct_of(c(mean(b$dep[b$year < 1981]), mean(b$dep[b$year >= 2011]))))
}))
for (id in ids) for (w in wb$window) {
  b <- yy[yy$site_id == id & yy$window == w & yy$route == "borrowed", ]
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(mean(b$dep[b$year >= 2011]) - mean(b$dep[b$year < 1981]), row_of(id, w, "carried")$change)))
}
```

```{r years, fig.height = 8.5, fig.cap = "Each window's mean flow, year by year, as a share of its 1981–2010 typical flow (log scale). Large orange points are measured summers; the grey line fills the other years from one nearby gauge, with its 90% range; the blue line is borrowed from nearby gauges' year-to-year departures. A small point is a year with no neighbouring year on its line. Black lines are the borrowed route's typical departure before 1981 and since 2011."}
ggplot(yy, aes(year)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = pal_series$values[["band"]]) +
  geom_ribbon(data = yl[yl$line == "filled", ], aes(ymin = pct_of(lo), ymax = pct_of(hi), fill = "band")) +
  geom_line(data = yl[yl$line == "filled", ], aes(y = pct, colour = "filled"), linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_line(data = yl[yl$line == "borrowed", ], aes(y = pct, colour = "borrowed"), linewidth = 0.35) +
  geom_linerange(data = yl[yl$alone & yl$line == "filled" & yl$route %in% "filled", ],
                 aes(ymin = pct_of(lo), ymax = pct_of(hi)), colour = pal_series$values[["band"]], linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(data = yl[yl$alone & yl$line == "filled" & yl$route %in% "filled", ], aes(y = pct, colour = "filled"),
             size = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = yl[yl$alone & yl$line == "borrowed", ], aes(y = pct, colour = "borrowed"), size = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = yy[yy$route == "measured", ], aes(y = pct, colour = "measured"), size = 1.2) +
  geom_segment(data = per, aes(x = x, xend = xend, y = y, yend = y, colour = "period_mean"), linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_grid(site ~ wlab, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(trans = scales::trans_new("pct_log", function(p) log1p(p / 100), function(z) 100 * expm1(z)),
                     breaks = c(-95, -90, -75, -50, 0, 100, 300), labels = function(p) paste0(100 + p, "%")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal_series$values["band"], labels = pal_series$labels["band"], name = NULL) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_series$values[c("measured", "filled", "borrowed", "period_mean")],
                      labels = pal_series$labels[c("measured", "filled", "borrowed", "period_mean")], name = NULL) +
  guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2), fill = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Share of typical 1981–2010 flow")
```

```{r change-numbers}
ext <- ch[ch$group == "BULK" & ch$statistic == "mean" & ch$window == "spawning" & ch$route == "extended", ]
stopifnot(nrow(ext) == 3, all(ext$pct < 0))
morr <- row_of("gosnell", "spawning", "carried", group = "MORR")
stopifnot(morr$pct < 0, morr$pct_hi > 0)
# "smaller" than under the Bulkley windows
stopifnot(abs(morr$pct) < abs(row_of("gosnell", "spawning", "carried")$pct))
# "whose spawning window falls a month later": the Morice spawning window starts 25-35 days after the Bulkley's
start_of <- function(g) as.Date(paste0("2001-", v$windows$start[v$windows$site_id == "gosnell" & v$windows$group == g &
                                                                 v$windows$window == "spawning"]))
stopifnot(as.numeric(start_of("MORR") - start_of("BULK")) %in% 25:35)
# the Morice windows, from the bundle; the spawning window opens in the first week of September and closes in the first of October
wm <- v$windows[v$windows$site_id == "gosnell" & v$windows$group == "MORR", c("window", "start", "end")]
stopifnot(identical(wm$window, c("migration", "spawning")), wm$start[2] %in% sprintf("09-%02d", 1:7),
          wm$end[2] %in% sprintf("10-%02d", 1:7))
# the ranking: largest at Maxan and Naver, smallest at Swift
rk <- spw$site_id[order(spw$pct)]
stopifnot(setequal(rk[1:2], c("maxan", "naver")), rk[length(rk)] == "swift")
```

The spawning-window drop is largest at Maxan and Naver creeks and smallest at Swift
Creek, and filling in each gauged stream's own record gives drops in the same direction
(`r pct(min(abs(ext$pct)))`–`r pct(max(abs(ext$pct)))`).

```{r change, fig.height = 4.2, fig.cap = "Change in each window's mean flow, from the years before 1981 to the years since 2011 (to 2024, or 2025 where recorded), with its 90% range, by each route the legend names."}
dd <- ch[ch$group == "BULK" & ch$statistic == "mean", ]
dd$site <- factor(name_of[dd$site_id], levels = rev(name_of[ids]))
dd$wlab <- factor(wlab[dd$window], levels = wlab)
ggplot(dd, aes(pct, site, colour = route)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = pal_series$values[["filled"]]) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = pct_lo, xmax = pct_hi), height = 0, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_point(size = 2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~wlab) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal_change$values, labels = pal_change$labels, name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Change in mean flow (%)", y = NULL)
```

Gosnell Creek also has Chinook windows of its own. Morice Chinook spawn from the first
week of September to the first week of October
([Bustard and Schell 2002](#ref-bustard2002), p. 27), so the Morice's spawning window,
`r md_text(wm$start[2])` to `r md_text(wm$end[2])`, falls a month later than the
Bulkley's. Under these windows Gosnell Creek's spawning-window drop is smaller,
`r pct(morr$pct)`, and its range reaches no change.

## How well does the method score?

```{r scores}
tab <- data.frame(
  Stream = name_of[sc$site_id],
  `Filled-in record` = sprintf("%.2f", sc$ols),
  `Gauges tested` = sc$ext_gauges,
  `Borrowed, migration` = sprintf("%.2f", ss_mig$carried[match(sc$site_id, ss_mig$site_id)]),
  `Borrowed, spawning` = sprintf("%.2f", ss_spw$carried[match(sc$site_id, ss_spw$site_id)]),
  `Gauges scored` = sc$carried_gauges,
  check.names = FALSE)
knitr::kable(tab, row.names = FALSE, align = "lrrrrr",
             caption = "Held-out scores of each window's mean flow, over the gauges in each stream's box: the median over gauges, where 1 is perfect and 0 is no better than the average year. The filled-in column is the migration window's; Gosnell Creek has no record of its own to fill in.")
stopifnot(sc$ols[sc$site_id == "swift"] < 0.2)
# "only N gauges" and "few long records": the upper Fraser box has the fewest
stopifnot(sc$ext_gauges[sc$site_id == "swift"] < min(sc$ext_gauges[sc$site_id != "swift"]))
# "the less certain of its two routes": Swift's filled-in range wider than its borrowed one, in both windows
width <- function(w, route) with(row_of("swift", w, route), pct_hi - pct_lo)
stopifnot(width("migration", "extended") > width("migration", "carried"),
          width("spawning", "extended") > width("spawning", "carried"))
```

Both routes are scored by hiding a gauge's own record and predicting it from its
neighbours. A score of 0.5 was set as the method's bar before any stream was run. The
borrowed departures clear it in the migration window in every box, and under these
spawning windows fall below it in every box, `r sprintf("%.2f", min(ss_spw$carried))`–`r sprintf("%.2f", max(ss_spw$carried))`;
their ranges in the change figure carry that weaker score. Filling in a record scores
about the same in the Bulkley, Cottonwood and Morice boxes, and poorly in the upper
Fraser, where only `r sc$ext_gauges[sc$site_id == "swift"]` gauges have records long
enough to test it; there, Swift Creek's change from its filled-in record is the less
certain of its two routes.

## Does snow explain it?

```{r snow}
sn <- v$snow[v$snow$group == "BULK" & v$snow$series == "carried" & v$snow$predictor == "swe", ]
sn_mig <- sn[sn$window == "migration", ]
sn_spw <- sn[sn$window == "spawning", ]
stopifnot(setequal(sn_mig$site_id, ids), setequal(sn_spw$site_id, ids))
# "at all four": each migration slope's 90% range above zero
stopifnot(all(sn_mig$lo > 0))
r2_mig <- range(sn_mig$r2)
r2_spw <- max(sn_spw$r2)
stopifnot(r2_spw < min(r2_mig) / 2)
# the melt date, the other snow predictor, over the spawning window
melt_spw <- v$snow[v$snow$group == "BULK" & v$snow$series == "carried" & v$snow$predictor == "doy" &
                     v$snow$window == "spawning", ]
stopifnot(setequal(melt_spw$site_id, ids))
r2_melt <- max(melt_spw$r2)
stopifnot(r2_melt < min(r2_mig))
```

The migration-window departures borrowed for each stream follow the winter's snow: in
years with more peak snow over its catchment they are higher, at all four with a 90%
range above zero, and peak snow alone accounts for
`r round(100 * r2_mig[1])`–`r round(100 * r2_mig[2])`% of their year-to-year spread. In
the spawning window it accounts for at most `r round(100 * r2_spw)`%, and the melt date
for at most `r round(100 * r2_melt)`%.

## Where could it be wrong?

```{r limits}
nerr <- v$normal[v$normal$group == "BULK" & v$normal$window == "spawning", ]
stopifnot(nrow(nerr) == 1, nerr$err_median > 0, nerr$err_q75 > nerr$err_median)
# the citation section names routed PCIC as Gosnell Creek's typical flow and as every hydrograph's source
stopifnot(all(v$normal$pick == "pcic_routed"), all(v$daily$source[v$daily$pick] == "pcic_routed"))
```

- **Gosnell Creek's flow is never measured.** Its departures are tested only at the
  gauges around it, and its typical flow is `wet`'s published flow for the stream. At
  `r nerr$err_n` gauges in its box with ten or more years of the 1981–2010 baseline, that
  published spawning-window flow runs a median `r pct(pct_of(nerr$err_median))` above
  measured, and about `r pct(pct_of(nerr$err_q75))` or more above at a quarter of them.
- **The windows are the Bulkley's** at all four streams. Only the Morice has its own cited
  windows; Swift and Naver creeks have none yet.
- **Each filled-in year rests on one neighbouring gauge**, and the earliest years on
  whichever single gauge reaches back that far.

## Software and citation

The flows in this article are from HYDAT release `r prov$hydat`; Gosnell Creek's typical
flow and the hydrographs are `wet`'s published daily flow (for these four streams, routed
PCIC's); the streams, lakes and catchments are the Freshwater Atlas's, through `fwapg`;
place names are BC Geographic Names'. The data were bundled at `wet` commit
`r prov$wet_commit`. How each stream was chosen, and how the method is run and scored, is
set out in
[`wet`'s research notes](https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/wet/blob/main/research/chinook_sites.md).

```{r citation, results = "asis"}
cat(wet:::wet_software_cite(c("wet", "cd", "ggplot2", "gq", "sf")), sep = "\n")
```

Cite `wet` by the DOI above, which resolves to its latest release.

### Data

- Daily flow: the Water Survey of Canada's HYDAT, release `r prov$hydat`.
- Typical flow at each stream (the hydrographs, and Gosnell Creek's normal): routed flow
  from the Pacific Climate Impacts Consortium, University of Victoria
  ([hydromosaic](https://beehive.pacificclimate.org/chyp/): VIC-GL hydrologic model output
  routed with Raven, PNWNAmet forcing), placed on the Freshwater Atlas by New Graph's fork
  of `fwapg` (Norris, S. and Irvine, A. (2026), *fwapg, New Graph Environment's fork*,
  <https://github.com/NewGraphEnvironment/fwapg/tree/newgraph>) and published by `wet`
  (build `r substr(v$normal$digest[1], 1, 7)`).
- Spawner surveys: Fisheries and Oceans Canada's New Salmon Escapement Database System
  (NuSEDS), release of 1 June 2026,
  <https://open.canada.ca/data/en/dataset/c48669a3-045b-400d-b730-48aafe8c5ee6>.
- Fish observations: Province of British Columbia, Known BC Fish Observations and BC Fish
  Distributions.
- Snow: ERA5-Land ([Muñoz-Sabater and others 2021](#ref-munoz2021)), summarised per year by
  `cd`.
- Streams, lakes and catchments: the Freshwater Atlas Stream Network (Province of British
  Columbia, 2021, <https://catalogue.data.gov.bc.ca/dataset/freshwater-atlas-stream-network>),
  held in a database by Norris, S. (2024), *fwapg*, <https://github.com/smnorris/fwapg>.
- Place names: BC Geographic Names.

- <span id="ref-bustard2002"></span>Bustard, D. and Schell, C. (2002). *Conserving Morice
  Watershed Fish Populations and Their Habitat*. Stage II Biophysical Profile,

  Community Futures Development Corporation of Nadina.
  <https://waves-vagues.dfo-mpo.gc.ca/Library/315091.pdf>
- <span id="ref-gottesfeld2007"></span>Gottesfeld, A.S. and Rabnett, K.A. (2007). *Skeena
  Fish Populations and Their Habitat*. Skeena Fisheries Commission.
- <span id="ref-munoz2021"></span>Muñoz-Sabater, J. and others (2021). ERA5-Land: a
  state-of-the-art global reanalysis dataset for land applications. *Earth System Science
  Data* 13, 4349–4383.
  [doi:10.5194/essd-13-4349-2021](https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-13-4349-2021)

```{r wordcount, include = FALSE}
f <- knitr::current_input()
if (!is.null(f)) {
  x <- readLines(f, warn = FALSE)
  y <- utils::tail(x, -utils::head(which(x == "---"), 2)[2])   # drop the YAML header
  cite <- which(y == "## Software and citation")
  stopifnot(length(cite) == 1)
  y <- utils::head(y, cite - 1)   # the closing citation section is not body prose
  fence <- cumsum(grepl("^```", y)) %% 2 == 1
  y <- y[!fence & !grepl("^```", y)]
  y <- gsub("`r [^`]*`", "", y)          # inline code is not body prose
  y <- y[!grepl("^\\s*$", y)]
  n <- sum(lengths(strsplit(trimws(y), "\\s+")))
  message("body prose: ", n, " words")
  cap <- 1000
  if (n > cap) stop("body prose is ", n, " words; the cap is ", cap)
}
```
